name: source-lists
text: Valid sources only. Primary: the entity the figure is about, on its own official domain, or the official record-keeper for that fact. Verifier: an independent auditor, index, registry or official dataset.

Never valid: statistics aggregators and SEO sites, blogs, forums, Wikipedia (follow its citation instead), modeled traffic estimators (Similarweb, Semrush), AI-generated pages, press releases distributed by third parties, and the founder own posts. A news story repeating a media-kit number is not a source.

Every figure needs its primary source plus a second valid source. When a verifier covers the fact the second source must be the verifier (independently confirmed); otherwise a separate official document from the same issuer (issuer-confirmed). Numbers must match within 25 percent and describe the same measure. Figures older than 12 months are re-researched.

Structured sources come first: the verifier APIs (OpenAlex, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, BLS, O*NET, ecosyste.ms, Hugging Face, SEC EDGAR) are queried before any web search, and web search is used only for figures no API holds. Official record-keepers (BLS, O*NET, SEC, USPTO) count as primary sources for their own records.
